column1: # Tier rules. One rule per line: REGEX <TAB> TIER <TAB> NOTE
# The FIRST matching rule decides a path's tier. A change's tier is the HIGHEST tier among its files.
# Automation can only RAISE a tier, never lower it (Temeller A1, article 9). The one deterministic
# exception is the meaning-preserving correction guard in tier.py (typos, formatting, link archiving),
# which can lower Tier 2 to Tier 1 but never Tier 3.
# Tier 1  Small, reversible changes. Merged by automation after a 72 h cooling period. Anyone can revert.
# Tier 2  Normative text. Needs a published AI referee (or panel) decision, an independent verification of the
#         diff, and an expired challenge window. Merged by automation (K31: no founder or board approval).
# Tier 3  The machine's own rules. Automation never opens or merges PRs that touch these paths. They are
#         enacted by a human custodian executing a published decision ("two keys"). No custodian: they stay frozen.
# Special tier token "1d": Tier 1 only for NEWLY ADDED translation files whose front matter says
# status: machine-draft or status: in-review. Otherwise Tier 2.
# Paths not matched by any rule are Tier 2 (safe default).
